clue.text: Plans to make 500 crude vessels

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
rafts are rough floating craft lashed together from logs or planks

explanation.surface: Someone means to build five hundred rough boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Drafts are preliminary versions or outlines of a scheme, so they are plans.

clue.text: Take no responsibility for underworld attempt to get insurance payout

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the name is used for the underworld itself
a claim is a request made to an insurer for money

explanation.surface: A gangster tries to collect on an insurance policy and then washes their hands of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests criminals, but it is the classical realm of the dead, called Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim something is to deny any connection with or liability for it.

clue.text: A pair of fellows taking on one crane? You could swear it

parts.note: F abbreviates fellow, so a pair of them is two Fs
I is the Roman numeral for one
a davit is a small crane on a ship, used for raising lifeboats

explanation.surface: Two men take on a single crane, and the claim is that you could swear to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking on' just links the pieces, which run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An affidavit is a written statement sworn on oath, so it is something one swears.

clue.text: To work in West African republic

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: Someone is posted to a job in a West African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a small republic on the Gulf of Guinea, between Ghana and Benin.

clue.text: Ecologist to eat out and drink

parts.note: a Green is an environmentalist, a member of an ecology party

indicators.note: out says the letters of eat are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An environmentalist goes out for a meal and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EAT into TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is an unfermented tea taken as a beverage.

clue.text: Have misgivings about first military construction

indicators.note: first says the piece for about goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
to doubt is to have misgivings

explanation.surface: An officer has second thoughts about the first fortification built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you the word for 'about' leads; read in surface order it would trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary fortification or stronghold built by soldiers.

clue.text: Pulling out old method of haulage

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in an ex-wife
traction is the pulling of a load, as by a traction engine

explanation.surface: A former way of hauling goods is being withdrawn from service.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraction is the act of drawing something out, like a tooth.

clue.text: Find a small amount

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a tiny quantity of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to track down or locate; a trace is also a tiny quantity, as in a trace of poison.

clue.text: Friend's going round English lanes

indicators.note: going round says the friend's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: an ally is a friend; with the possessive it gives ally plus S

explanation.surface: A pal walks round some English country lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts E inside ALLYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are narrow passages or back streets, so they are lanes.

clue.text: Occupy oneself somewhat dilettantishly as a novelist? Not right

indicators.note: not right says R, the abbreviation for right, is dropped

parts.note: Margaret Drabble is an English novelist

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a writer only playing at it is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' removes R from DRABBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dabble is to take up an activity casually and without serious commitment, as an amateur would.

clue.text: South American fellow argued about precaution

indicators.note: about says the letters of argued are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A man from South America has been debating a protective measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ARGUED into EGUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A safeguard is a measure taken to protect against harm, which is a precaution.

clue.text: Scenic route taken by the northern public transport

parts.note: in northern English dialect, especially Yorkshire, 'the' is shortened to t'
rail is the railway as a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A pretty route is followed by the train in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path through countryside, often a marked route for walkers.

clue.text: liquid

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'liquid (4)', starting lower case, so it is cut short; no wordplay for LADE survives and no scan or search gives the rest.

clue.text: Old boy routinely limits speed in an obstinate way

parts.note: OB abbreviates old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: limits says the routine word encloses the next piece on both sides

parts.note: duly means as expected or in the usual way
a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: A former pupil keeps strictly to the speed limit every time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' is a container signal here, not a speed limit: the word for 'routinely' wraps the word for 'speed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurately means stubbornly, refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Maybe chronic bit of inflammation in the chest?

indicators.note: maybe says the letters are only possibly in this order and should be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor wonders whether a little chest inflammation is long-term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges CHRONIC and BIT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronchitic describes a person or condition affected by bronchitis, an inflammation of the airways in the lungs.

clue.text: The opposite of what's written as prose?

definitions.text: The opposite of what's written as prose?

parts.words: The opposite of what's written as prose?
parts.note: the opposite of prose is poetry, so something not in prose is written in lines of poetry, and the two words joined also mean reversed

explanation.surface: A question about what counts as the opposite of prose.
explanation.walkthrough: As one word the answer means opposite; split in two it says written as poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means opposite, and split as two words it means in poetic form, the reverse of prose.

clue.text: Small flier came first with appellation

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
led means was in front, came first

explanation.surface: A small bird won the race and earned a name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titled means having a title, a name or rank by which someone is called.

clue.text: Europe's acidity measure is evaluating river

parts.note: EU abbreviates the European Union, standing for Europe
pH is the scale used to measure acidity
rates means is assessing or valuing

explanation.surface: Europe is checking how acidic a river is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a major river of western Asia, flowing through Turkey, Syria and Iraq.

clue.text: Teacher with English coin, gold

parts.note: a ducat is an old European gold coin
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A teacher has an English coin made of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is someone who instructs others, which is a teacher.

clue.text: Lines of fittest Anzacs

indicators.note: of says the answer is drawn out from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A poem about the fittest Australian and New Zealand soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: ANZACs are soldiers of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem.

clue.text: Flying structure shown in broadcast's trendy

parts.note: broadcast is: airs means broadcasts, as a programme airs
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable flying craft appears on a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast's' means 'broadcast is', giving AIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a lighter-than-air craft with an engine, a structure that flies.

clue.text: Picked up news exclusive followed up by journalist

parts.note: a scoop is a story published by one paper before its rivals
ED abbreviates editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter took up a big exclusive story and chased it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scooped means lifted or gathered up, as with a spoon or the hands.

clue.text: Do wrong going to gully oddly unaccompanied

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong

indicators.note: oddly says take the letters in the odd positions of the word gully

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves by going off down a gully on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps the first, third and fifth letters of 'gully'.
explanation.definitionFit: Singly means one by one or on one's own, without company.

clue.text: Some fowl is hooting? Not entirely typical of it!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird is hooting, which is not quite what that sort of bird does.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' is the hooting fowl, an owl; owlish means somewhat like an owl, hence 'Not entirely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Owlish means resembling an owl to some degree, so it is partly typical of the hooting bird.

clue.text: We'll get a call about article coming through

parts.note: the clue's we will supplies WE as written

indicators.note: about says the call surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a ring is a telephone call
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone expects a phone call about a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal, not 'concerning'; 'coming through' is the definition, as in weathering a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Weathering a storm means coming through it safely, surviving it.

clue.text: Psychiatrist given promotion to lecturer with little hesitation

parts.note: an ad is a promotion or advertisement
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist is promoted to lecturer after only a moment's hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Adler was an Austrian psychiatrist, founder of individual psychology.

clue.text: Aquatic reptile seen around in Languedoc or Camargue

indicators.note: around says the letters found are read in the opposite direction
in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A crocodile is spotted somewhere in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Camargue is a marshy delta in Provence; the run CORC spans 'Languedoc or Camargue' and is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A croc is short for crocodile, a large reptile that lives in water.

clue.text: Runs on to blade, giving shout

parts.note: R abbreviates runs in cricket scoring
the blade of an oar is its flat end, and blade stands for the whole oar

explanation.surface: A rower makes a shout as they reach for their blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A roar is a loud, deep shout.

clue.text: Land in the main has a tenant

explanation.surface: An island in the ocean is rented out to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the open sea, an old poetic term; split, the answer reads IS LET.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island in the sea; 'is let' means is rented out to a tenant.

clue.text: Hostile at changes to instrument for reflecting sun

indicators.note: changes to says these letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A hostile reaction to a solar mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes to' rearranges HOSTILE and AT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliostat is a device with a mirror that tracks the sun and reflects its light in a fixed direction.

clue.text: A print-out difficult to plagiarise?

parts.note: hard means difficult
to copy is to plagiarise someone else's work

explanation.surface: A printed document that is hard to pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard copy is the printed paper version of a computer document.

clue.text: Short sermon — after time, something serving to aid correction?

indicators.note: after says the shortened sermon follows the time piece

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: short says the word sermon is cut down to its opening three letters

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A brief sermon, preached after a while, meant to put sinners right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last three letters of 'sermon', a heavier trim than usual; 'after time' sets that stub behind the period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser rubs out mistakes, a tool for making corrections.
